case_studies.title: IDP AutoOpt: Agent-Driven Optimization of Document Processing Pipeline Configurations
case_studies.abstract: We present IDP AutoOpt, an autonomous LLM agent that discovers high-performing configurations for intelligent document processing (IDP) pipelines. Tuning IDP prompts, models, OCR settings, and schemas jointly currently costs domain specialists 20 to 80+ person-hours per document type and does not scale as enterprises add document classes. IDP AutoOpt runs a closed loop: it scores a configuration on a small labeled set, diagnoses field-level errors, generates targeted edits, and re-evaluates, guided by human-authored domain skills that encode production expertise. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of manually optimizing document processing pipelines, which can take up to 80+ hours per document type. The researchers built an autonomous agent called IDP AutoOpt that can automatically discover high-performing configurations. The result is a significant reduction in the time and effort required to optimize these pipelines.
case_studies.it_breakdown: If you manage document processing pipelines, here is what to do: review your current optimization process, consider implementing an autonomous agent like IDP AutoOpt, and evaluate the potential time and cost savings it could bring to your organization.
case_studies.score_reasoning: Relevance to IT infrastructure, novelty in automating IDP pipeline optimization, and potential to save IT engineers time by automating labor-intensive tasks within 90 days.

case_studies.title: Stop Shipping AI Agents on Faith: Capability Is Not Production Readiness
case_studies.abstract: AI agents are moving into production workflows where they retrieve information, call tools, maintain state, and act on behalf of users or organizations, but many release decisions still rely on capability signals, demos, or behavioral tests that do not show whether an agent is ready to operate under production constraints. Capability is therefore not production readiness. This paper introduces the ProofAgent Index (PAI), a governance readiness index for AI agents. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of AI agents not being production-ready despite having capabilities, by introducing the ProofAgent Index (PAI), a governance readiness index that evaluates AI agents' deployment evidence. The researchers built the PAI, which combines four dimensions of deployment evidence. The result is a more reliable way to determine if an AI agent is ready for production use.
case_studies.it_breakdown: If you manage AI agent deployments, here is what to do: assess your current deployment process, check if it covers the four dimensions of the PAI (Evaluation, Context, Compliance, and Governance), and adjust your process to include these dimensions to ensure production readiness. This flags a risk: if your organization uses AI agents in production workflows, check your deployment process immediately to avoid potential issues. Not directly applicable to general IT infrastructure work, but relevant to AI agent deployment.
case_studies.relevance_tag: Gemini relevance tag: AI engineering, IT operations
case_studies.score_reasoning: Novel approach to measuring AI production readiness, directly addresses IT concerns with LLM and agentic systems, actionable insights for IT teams.

case_studies.title: MerchantBench: Benchmarking LLM Agents for Long-Term Coherence in E-Commerce Operations
case_studies.abstract: Large language model agents are increasingly evaluated as autonomous tool users, yet most benchmarks focus on bounded tasks with immediate success criteria. Real-world deployments often require Long-Term Coherence, the capacity to preserve purposeful behavior across extended horizons while adapting decisions to accumulated evidence. Evaluating this capacity requires a persistent environment in which actions constrain future choices, feedback arrives at heterogeneous delays, and incoherent behavior produces measurable cumulative effects. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of evaluating large language model agents' ability to preserve purposeful behavior over time in real-world deployments, the authors built a benchmarking tool called MerchantBench, and the result is a persistent environment to test long-term coherence in e-commerce operations. The tool evaluates language model agents' capacity to adapt decisions based on accumulated evidence. This research is focused on e-commerce and language model agents, not directly related to cloud infrastructure management.

case_studies.title: Beyond Component Testing: Validating Agentic AI Systems
case_studies.abstract: Agentic AI systems act through multi-step trajectories that combine planning, tool use, memory, interaction, and adaptation. This behavior stretches validation practice beyond component testing and one-shot input--output evaluation, because acceptable system behavior now depends on how decisions unfold over time and under changing environmental conditions. This survey synthesizes 257 papers spanning agent evaluation, software assurance, cyber-physical systems, runtime monitoring, and regulatory guidance in order to characterize the validation problem for agentic systems. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of validating AI systems that make decisions over time and adapt to changing conditions. The authors built a survey of 257 papers to understand the validation challenges for these systems. The result is a characterization of the validation problem for agentic AI systems.
case_studies.it_breakdown: Not directly applicable to IT infrastructure work, as it focuses on validating AI systems rather than managing cloud infrastructure. If your organization is involved in developing or implementing agentic AI systems, this research may be relevant to your development team. It does not directly impact cloud infrastructure management.
case_studies.score_reasoning: Paper abstract does not provide direct relevance or actionable information for IT engineers or consultants, but does hint at the need for novel validation methods in AI systems. IT relevance is low due to lack of focus on specific tools or deployment scenarios.

case_studies.title: Simulation Code Generation for Fluid Systems using Large Language Models: Benchmarking Models and Prompting Strategies
case_studies.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have demonstrated a strong ability to generate syntactically correct code from natural-language specifications. In this study, we explore how LLMs can be harnessed to automatically translate a neutral graph representation of fluid system models into executable code for two widely adopted simulation environments: the Python library WNTR and the Modelica Standard Library. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of manually translating fluid system models into executable code by building a system that uses large language models to automatically generate simulation code. They built a system that can translate graph representations into code for two simulation environments. The result is a systematic comparison of different language models and prompting strategies to find the most effective approach.

case_studies.title: Benchmarking the Residual: What Long-Horizon Evaluations Add Beyond Matched Short-Task Performance
case_studies.abstract: Long-horizon benchmarks often show that agents fail more as tasks become longer. This observation is useful for deployment, but it does not by itself explain why failure occurs. More stages create more opportunities for ordinary errors to compound; longer tasks may also contain harder individual decisions or become harder as conversation history, tool outputs, and environment changes accumulate. We use trajectory-induced degradation to mean this last possibility: earlier execution makes later work harder. case_studies.summary: This research investigates why artificial intelligence models fail more often in longer tasks, and what causes this failure. The authors built a benchmark to evaluate long-horizon performance and identified that earlier execution can make later work harder. This research is not directly relevant to IT infrastructure work.
case_studies.it_breakdown: Not directly applicable to IT infrastructure work. If your organisation uses AI models for tasks, this research may be of interest to data scientists or AI developers, but it does not require immediate action from IT infrastructure teams. No specific action is required to apply this research to IT infrastructure management.
